articles.title: England’s Alex Mitchell out of Nations Championship with fourth hamstring injury in 2026
articles.summary: Jack van Poortvliet expected to start against Australia. Fin Smith also an injury concern to Steve Borthwick. Alex Mitchell has been ruled out of all of England’s Nations Championship campaign as a result of his latest hamstring injury, dealing a significant blow to Steve Borthwick before the…
body: The Northampton scrum-half had already been deemed unavailable for the clash against the Wallabies and a scan on Monday has determined that Mitchell will sit out all of England’s autumn campaign.

As a result, Jack van Poortvliet is expected to start at scrum-half against Australia with Ben Spencer and Harry Randall vying for a spot on the bench. For Mitchell, however, it is rotten luck given it is the fourth time this year he has sustained a hamstring injury.

He picked up similar injuries during the Six Nations, at an England camp in May – recovering to take his place in the Northampton squad for the Prem final win against Exeter – and during the summer Test against Fiji. Van Poortvliet was England’s starting scrum-half for the summer given Mitchell’s lack of game time but when fit and firing the Northampton Saint is England’s first-choice No 9.

articles.title: Falling revenues, bigger losses, higher wages: Prem Rugby clubs’ debt climbs to £366m
articles.summary: Six clubs found to be balance-sheet insolvent. Spending restraint urged despite investment. Prem Rugby clubs’ collective losses and debt levels are continuing to increase despite growing interest from global companies and financiers shown by the recent investment of Red Bull, Sir James Dyson, and…
body: The third edition of the Leonard Curtis Rugby Finance Report published on Tuesday shows that the financial losses of the 10 Prem clubs rose from £34m to £36.5m over the 2024-25 season and combined debt levels increased from £342.5m to £366.1m, while the top flight’s total wage bills grew from £125.9m to £129.8m, 80% of revenues.

The impact of this increased spending was compounded by a decline in revenues from £182.2m to £178.9m, with the result that six of the 10 clubs are balance-sheet insolvent with Northampton, Gloucester, Leicester and Saracens the only exceptions.

The report from Leonard Curtis, a leading UK corporate recovery and insolvency firm, is compiled using publicly available figures for the 2024-25 season and echoes its findings in previous years of a sport overly reliant on owner funding leading to concerns over the long-term sustainability of many clubs.

All 10 Prem Rugby clubs are in debt with their average losses totalling £3.7m annually or £308,000 a month and Alex Cadwallader, a Leonard Curtis directorand former England under-21 international, says major structural change is needed.

articles.title: Saliba's back for Arsenal - how does Arteta solve his defensive dilemma?
articles.summary: William Saliba returning to first-team training before Arsenal's game with Slavia Prague in the Champions League is a huge boost for the club but now presents Mikel Arteta with a selection headache.
body: But it is one that will be both welcome to the Arsenal boss and the envy of other top teams across the continent.

That's because William Saliba - a key figure in the Gunners' title win last season - is back in training, having missed the entire campaign so far because of a back injury following his early withdrawal in France's World Cup semi-final loss to Spain.

The 25-year-old has been one of the Premier League's top defenders in recent seasons but - in his absence - summer signing Ezri Konsa has stepped in seamlessly to help Arsenal back to the top of the table.

Indeed, since Konsa's arrival from Aston Villa for £55m, he and Gabriel Magalhaes have struck up a formidable partnership, with Arsenal again boasting the league's tightest defence, conceding just five goals in nine games.

articles.title: Giannis says Dončić could be best scorer of all time as Lakers star pours in 42 against Heat
articles.summary: Slovenian star is averaging 38.3 points per game. Antetokounmpo offers high praise to fellow All-Star. Giannis Antetokounmpo has offered high praise to his fellow All-Star Luka Dončić after the Los Angeles Lakers star went on another scoring tear on Monday night.
body: Dončić scored 42 points in the Lakers’ 138-117 win over Antetokounmpo’s Heat to bring the Slovene’s scoring average this season to 38.3 points per game, the best in the NBA.

“Obviously, he’s one of the best scorers to play this game, if not the best,” Antetokounmpo said. Antetokounmpo was asked to clarify his answer and replied: “Not right now. Of all time. I feel like some people are scared to say that, but he’s got to be up there.”

Dončić’s career scoring average of 29.35 points per game trails only those of Michael Jordan (30.12) and Wilt Chamberlain (30.07). He is 165th on the all-time points list at 15,289, but he is still only 27.
The Lakers are 6-2 to start the season and Dončić is averaging 43.4 points over the last five games.

articles.title: 24-year-old woman dies after collapsing in final stages of New York City Marathon
articles.summary: Father says Rachel Apa died from rhabdomyolysis. Runner was former college athlete in ‘perfect shape’ A 24-year-old woman died after collapsing during the final stages of Sunday’s New York City Marathon, her father has said.
body: Rachel Apa’s father, Steve Apa, told the New York Times his daughter was in Central Park, two miles from the end of the race, when she collapsed. It was Rachel’s first marathon and she was running as part of the Parkinson’s Champions team in honor of her late grandfather, who suffered from the disease.
Steve Apa told the Times that his daughter had played field hockey at college and was in “perfect health, perfect shape”.
Rachel, from Lewisberry, Pennsylvania, was being cheered on by Steve and her mother, Michelle Apa, on Sunday.

Michelle Apa filmed her daughter smiling at mile 14, but at mile 18 later Rachel texted her father, writing “Ow”. A mile later she texted him: “Ow, ow”. She appeared to have rallied when she texted “final stretch” to Steve at the 23rd mile. However, she collapsed soon afterwards and was given CPR by a member of the public. Race medical staff then used a defibrillator on Rachel, before she was taken to Mount Sinai Medical Center. Doctors there tried to save her but she died at 9.40pm. Her father told the Times that Rachel had died from rhabdomyolysis, a rare condition that can be brought on by heavy exercise in which muscles break down.

articles.title: Scrum, foul play, TMO - what can we expect from refs this autumn?
articles.summary: World Rugby has laid out a vision of a safer and more continuous sport, but with a desire to "embrace the contest" around the breakdown and set-piece.
body: The number of tries in international rugby has rocketed from six to eight per match in the space of just two years as World Rugby looks to futureproof the game.

As part of the manifesto, the sport's world governing body will ramp up fan engagement and has launched a study using biometric sensors to find out what excites and invigorates supporters during matches.
Before the return of the Nations Championship, the top 24 international head coaches met with World Rugby officials outside London to discuss how the game will look over the coming month.
According to World Rugby sources, the coaches highlighted a number of "grey areas"; for example the scrum and breakdown, deliberate knock-ons and foul play in the act of scoring.

articles.title: Mitchell ruled out of England’s Nations Championship
articles.summary: England have been dealt a blow with Alex Mitchell ruled out of the entire Nations Championship after sustaining a hamstring injury during Northampton’s 28-14 victory over Gloucester on Saturday.
body: The British and Irish Lions scrum-half underwent a scan on Monday, with the results confirming he will miss all four of this month's Tests.

It is the fourth hamstring injury Mitchell has sustained in 2026, dealing another setback to the scrum-half, who had been expected to play a key role in England's matches against Australia, Japan and New Zealand, as well as the Nations Championship finals weekend from November 27-29.

Jack van Poortvliet is now likely to start in the No 9 jersey for England's clash against the Wallabies on Sunday at the Allianz Stadium, with either Ben Spencer or Harry Randall providing cover from the bench.
Mitchell's Northampton team-mate Fin Smith is facing a race against time to be fit for Sunday's match, as he battles his second calf problem of the year.

He took part, however, in running drills on arrival in camp, with England sources remaining optimistic about his chances of being fit for Sunday's showdown with the Wallabies.
But the news around Mitchell had been expected ever since he withdrew in the first half of Northampton's 28-14 victory over the Cherry and Whites.

articles.title: King's former horse Point Of Law wins Melbourne Cup
articles.summary: Point Of Law, previously owned by the King and Queen, ran out a decisive winner of a Ciaron Maher dominated Lexus Melbourne Cup in Flemington.
body: Ciaron Maher continued his outstanding recent record in major races, training Point Of Law to Lexus Melbourne Cup glory at Flemington on Tuesday; stablemates Zahrann and Juja Kibo filled the places.

Seen as a St Leger hope after finishing fourth in the Queen's Vase at Royal Ascot and winning Newmarket's Bahrain Trophy for former trainers John and Thady Gosden, he was bought privately to continue his career in Australia, winning the Geelong Cup on his first outing for new connections.

With stablemate Royal Supremacy setting a strong pace for the big-race favourite to aim at, the son of Frankel showed a deadly turn of foot to run down the eventual fifth as Maher trained not only the first three home but also the fifth and sixth in the 'race that stops the nation'.

Maher told Australia's Channel Nine: "I knew I had my best hand going into it, but it's got to execute. I certainly didn't know Royal Supremacy was going to lead by that far but there's nothing better than a true staying test.

articles.title: Reynolds: Williams and Bears are 'complete' Super Bowl contenders
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears told us exactly who they think they are late last week when they traded for all-pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans.
body: The Bears gave up first-round draft picks in 2027 and 2028 for a 29-year-old defender. They may believe that due to their successes on the field those will be late first-round picks, but it's still a big price for a player who is not exactly young in NFL terms.

That suggested the Bears believe they are all-in. They were 5-2 when they made that trade and they thought they could upgrade a defense that actually started this season pretty well but had room for improvement.

On Monday night the Bears backed up that big trade and maybe sent another message to the rest of the NFL and the viewing public as they went into Seattle and recorded an emphatic 34-17 win over the hometown Seahawks, and Simmons made an impact immediately. He led the team with six tackles, had a sack, two tackles were for a loss and he batted down a pass.
This Bears team more importantly looks complete now. They're led by a head coach who is imaginative, aggressive and has just enough crazy in him to keep this team on the edge in Ben Johnson.

articles.title: Lions try to turn page to Dolphins with Jack Campbell on their minds
articles.summary: Head coach Dan Campbell says linebacker Jack Campbell is improving as the Lions manage several other injuries ahead of Sunday's game in Miami.
body: The Detroit Lions are trying to turn the page while keeping linebacker Jack Campbell in their thoughts.

The Lions are five days out from a game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 8. As Jack Campbell continues to trend in a positive direction, according to head coach Dan Campbell, the team has to regroup for a two-game road swing, including a trip to Munich, Germany, for a game against the New England Patriots on Nov. 15.
"The good news is he's improving," Dan Campbell said of Jack Campbell on Tuesday morning, Nov. 3, on the Costa & Jansen with Heather on 97.1 The Ticket.

"But we also got a job to do. This is what we're tasked with, and there's a reason why we go through all this stuff, you know, and it's to get to where we want to go collectively as a team, and you know, adversity comes in all shapes and sizes, and we've gotta overcome everything that finds our way.

articles.summary: Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here. Upheaval in the Indiana Fever front office could trickle down to the bench -- where Stephanie White has done an admirable job in trying circumstances over the past two seasons.
body: Fever's Stephanie White could get fresh start amid WNBA coaching shakeup originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

White's return to the Fever bench in 2025 brought with it renewed hopes of a first Indiana championship since 2012. The injury-wracked Fever reached the semifinals in White's first season back in Indy before they suffered a first-round exit to the Las Vegas Aces last month.

That triggered the departure of team president Kelly Krauskopf -- which had been anticipated. It also saw the Fever dismiss general manager Amber Cox, after a bombshell report in The Athletic laid bare the image issues that Indiana has faced around the league.

White herself has felt the strain of coaching Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and the Fever, who are the WNBA's biggest draw -- and who have been slammed for failing to get a grip on the toxicity coursing through their fanbase.
